findings.summary: configurehelp.pm bakes temp conversion-time paths that break the Perl test infrastructure
findings.evidence: cmake: tests/CMakeLists.txt:84-103 dynamically builds $Cpreprocessor from ${CMAKE_C_COMPILER} and INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES of the selected library target. Bazel gen_tests_configurehelp_pm (elements/curl/BUILD.bazel line 278) hard-codes '$Cpreprocessor = \'"​/usr/bin/cc" -E -I/tmp/curl/include -I/tmp/convert-element-build-1910530120/lib -I/tmp/curl/lib\'' — the path /tmp/convert-element-build-1910530120/lib is the ephemeral conversion sandbox's build directory where curl_config.h was generated; it does not exist in a real Bazel build. Any test that invokes the C preprocessor through configurehelp.pm (e.g. protocol-level tests that expand macros) will fail to find curl_config.h.

findings.summary: Public headers (include/curl/*.h) not in any pkg_files install target
findings.evidence: cmake: install(DIRECTORY "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/include/curl" DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}) at CMakeLists.txt:2261. elements/curl/include/BUILD.bazel exposes a cc_library :include_headers but no pkg_files rule installs those headers anywhere.

findings.summary: curl executable not in any pkg_files install target
findings.evidence: cmake: install(TARGETS curl DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}) at src/CMakeLists.txt:132. Bazel elements/curl/BUILD.bazel has exactly one pkg_files rule (install_files__bin, line 622) which covers only scripts/mk-ca-bundle.pl — no pkg_files for the curl cc_binary.

findings.summary: libcurl_static library not in any pkg_files install target
findings.evidence: cmake: install(TARGETS ${LIB_STATIC} EXPORT … ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}) at lib/CMakeLists.txt:272. Bazel elements/curl/BUILD.bazel has no pkg_files rule covering the libcurl_static cc_library output.

findings.summary: curl-config script generated but not installed
findings.evidence: cmake: CMakeLists.txt:2224-2227 generates curl-config via configure_file and then install(FILES "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/curl-config" DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}). Bazel produces gen_curl_config (elements/curl/BUILD.bazel line 293) as a write_file rule with visibility private, but there is no pkg_files rule pointing at that output.

findings.summary: libcurl.pc pkg-config file generated but not installed
findings.evidence: cmake: CMakeLists.txt:2255-2258 generates libcurl.pc via configure_file and then install(FILES "${PROJECT_BINARY_DIR}/libcurl.pc" DESTINATION "${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/pkgconfig"). Bazel produces gen_libcurl_pc (elements/curl/BUILD.bazel line 502) as a write_file rule with visibility private, but no pkg_files rule covers it.

findings.summary: curltool (unit-test lib) missing linkopts for ${CURL_LIBS} system libraries
findings.evidence: cmake src/CMakeLists.txt:104: target_link_libraries(curltool PRIVATE ${CURL_LIBS}). Bazel elements/curl/src/BUILD.bazel :curltool cc_library (line 180) has no linkopts for -lssl -lcrypto -lz and does not dep on :libcurl_static. Existing unit tests supply these linkopts directly, masking the gap.

findings.summary: curlu (unit-test lib) missing linkopts for ${CURL_LIBS} system libraries
findings.evidence: cmake lib/CMakeLists.txt:57: target_link_libraries(curlu PRIVATE ${CURL_LIBS}), which resolves to -lssl -lcrypto -lz (and any other backend libs). Bazel elements/curl/lib/BUILD.bazel :curlu cc_library (line 11) has no linkopts and no link_libraries for these system deps. Consumers (unit test binaries) happen to carry the flags themselves today, but the encapsulation is broken: new unit test targets that dep only on :curlu will fail to link.

findings.summary: CMAKE_DEBUG_POSTFIX "-d" not reflected in Bazel output names — debug builds produce libcurl_static.a instead of libcurl_staticd.a
findings.evidence: cmake CMakeLists.txt:244-247 sets CMAKE_DEBUG_POSTFIX to "-d", so cmake debug builds produce libcurld.a / curld (the curl exe gets a -d suffix too via CMAKE_DEBUG_POSTFIX). Bazel cc_library/cc_binary names are static strings with no per-config suffix, so the debug variant is identically named to the release variant. This makes it impossible to install both in the same prefix simultaneously, which cmake explicitly supported.
